You-ward
yoo'ward
prep. phrase (toward you; in your direction)
From you and the Saxon directional ending -weard, toward. The companion form to us-ward, and like it, preserved in English now only in the Authorized Version. This suffix is not the noun ward (watch, custody, prison, as in Gen 40:4); the two words are unrelated, and the dictionary keeps a separate entry for that one.

Biblical Definition

All three occurrences are Paul's, and all three are about the direction of a ministry. His conduct: “our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward” (2Co 1:12) — Paul lived plainly everywhere and most plainly toward the church that trusted him. His authority: “Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you” (2Co 13:3) — the Corinthians wanted evidence that Christ spoke through him, and Paul answers that the proof is aimed at them and already at work in them. And his commission: “If ye have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me to you-ward” (Eph 3:2) — the stewardship he received was not a general office but a grace given for them, the Gentiles. In each case the little suffix rules out a ministry that exists for itself. Conduct, authority, and calling are all described as pointed at particular people, and that is the New Testament pattern of office.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) notes that the termination ward, from Saxon weard, denotes direction toward, as in the Scripture phrases us-ward and you-ward, now obsolete in common speech.

expand to see more

WARD, a termination [Sax. weard], denotes direction or tendency to; as in toward, forward, homeward.

The grace of God which is given me to you-ward. Eph. 3.

Which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you. 2 Cor. 13.

The compound of a pronoun with this termination is peculiar to the older English and is retained in the common version of the Scriptures.

It answers to the Greek eis, unto or toward.

Key Scripture

2 Corinthians 1:12 — "For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward."

Ephesians 3:2 — "If ye have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me to you-ward:"

2 Corinthians 13:3 — "Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you."

1 Corinthians 9:2 — "If I be not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you: for the seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord."

Modern Corruption

Ministry has been detached from a particular people, so that a man may have an audience and no flock, and influence with no one to answer to.

expand to see more

The whole force of you-ward is particularity. Paul's conduct, his authority, and his very commission are described as pointed at named congregations, and 1 Corinthians 9:2 makes the logic explicit: the seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord. The proof of his office was the existence of the people it had produced. The broadcast era has made the opposite arrangement normal — a teaching ministry with an enormous audience and no congregation, accountable to no elders, producing followers no one is responsible for. The dictionary does not condemn the wide dissemination of sound teaching; it notes that the New Testament never treats it as a substitute for a man being toward a particular people.

2 Corinthians 1:12 supplies the other half, which is the transparency that particularity requires. Paul says he behaved in simplicity and godly sincerity in the world and more abundantly toward them — the people who could actually check. A ministry aimed at a real congregation is one in which the members can see the man's ordinary life, his money, his household, and his temper. That is precisely why the qualifications for eldership in 1 Timothy 3 are almost entirely domestic and observable. Where no one is in a position to verify, the qualifications cannot be applied, and the office has quietly become something else.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek pros humas (G4314), toward you; eis humas (G1519), unto you; oikonomia (G3622), stewardship, dispensation; Saxon weard, toward.

expand to see more

Greek pros humas (G4314) — toward you, face-to-face with you; 2 Corinthians 1:12.

Greek eis humas (G1519) — unto you; Ephesians 3:2, of the grace given for them.

Greek oikonomia (G3622) — household management, stewardship; the dispensation of grace Paul received.

Greek dokime (G1382) — proof, tested evidence; 2 Corinthians 13:3, what the Corinthians demanded.

Greek sphragis (G4973) — a seal; 1 Corinthians 9:2, the congregation itself as the proof of the office.

Usage

"“More abundantly to you-ward” — plainest before the people who could check."

"“The grace of God which is given me to you-ward” — a commission with an address on it."

"“The seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord” — the people are the proof."
